newsitem.title: ITALY: Brief guide to Italy's local elections on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Brief guide to Italy's local elections on Sunday.

text.p: Italy holds local elections on Sunday in the biggest test of voter support since Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left Olive Tree coalition won a general election victory on April 21, 1996.
Following is a brief guide to the contest.

-- The elections are for mayors and local councils in 1,115 towns and cities, including Milan and Turin in the north and Catania in Sicily. Voting will also take place for six provincial councils. In larger centres, a run-off will be held on May 11 between the two leading contenders for mayor in places where no candidate obtains an absolute majority on Sunday.
-- The eligible electorate is 9.47 million voters, about one fifth of the national total.
-- Polling stations open at seven a.m. (0500 GMT) and close at 10 p.m. (2000 GMT).
-- Italy's main television broadcasters, RAI and Fininvest, say they plan to carry exit polls by the forecasting organisation Abacus as soon as voting ends.
-- The official counts will begin at eight a.m. (0600 GMT) on Monday April 28. Final results are expected at around eight p.m. (1800 GMT) on Monday.
